transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie, Sofia, Ethan, Priya, Marcus, Hannah, Luis

Auto Summary (auto-generated): quick sync to align infra + product on the launch guardrails for the new 4x model variant; focus on smoke tests, regression signals, and capacity onramp steps.

--- Transcript ---
00:00:00 Jamie: ok everyone good morning, let's kick off, uh, thanks for joining, I know it's early for some folks
00:00:08 Sofia: morning, yep, good to go, I pulled the staging logs this morning, a few things to flag
00:00:13 Ethan: quick note from product side, timeline's compressed — we want a beta in three weeks so we need a crisp onramp
00:00:20 Jamie: right, so agenda — playbook outline, smoke test plan, regression signals matrix, ownership and dates. does that cover?
00:00:27 Luis: and release gating, don't forget the gating checklist, last time we missed a telemetry export which caused confusion
00:00:33 Marcus: mm-hmm, telemetry export should be part of the canary step, agree
00:00:38 Hannah: also QA needs stable prompt sets, not the ad-hoc ones, otherwise the regression numbers are noisy
00:00:44 Jamie: good, alright, playbook first — Priya you want to run the infra sequence?
00:00:50 Priya: yeah, quick overview. step one: provision canary pool sized for ~5% sustained traffic or N GPUs (we used 6 A100 equiv last time), step two: run a 48 hour burn-in with synthetic load + provenance tracing, step three: run customer-origin smoke tests against canary, collect lat/quant/cost metrics, step four: stage gradual ramp 5/15/50/100 with SLO checks and automatic rollback on regressions.
00:01:20 Sofia: couple clarifications — when you say "synthetic load" do you mean classic loadgen or mixed-mode with prefix caching enabled? we saw different lat profiles
00:01:28 Priya: mixed-mode, because prefix/KV cache changes behavior. run both with prefix warm and cold windows in the burn-in so we can see tails
00:01:37 Marcus: and capture KV hit-ratio, per-token latency p95/p99, convo length distribution, and cost per 1000 tokens, that's the set we'll use for gating
00:01:45 Ethan: product will add quality checks — hallucination rate on defined prompt sets and top-k consistency — those are the regressions that will block rollout
00:01:54 Hannah: to be explicit, QA needs: labeled pass/fail per prompt, notes about model truncation or cutoff, and a flakiness flag when results vary across runs
00:02:03 Jamie: okay, so regression signals set includes latency p99, KV hit ratio, hallucination rate, top-k consistency, and per-token cost delta. any objections?
00:02:12 Sofia: can we add memory pressure events as a signal? if the runtime OOMs even transiently that's a hard stop
00:02:17 Priya: yes add memory pressure and OOM spikes, also sustained GC or kernel fallback rates above X% should be considered a block
00:02:25 Marcus: how do we quantify "above X%" — suggest thresholds: p99 latency > 2x baseline, cost > 20% delta, hallucination rate increase > 3 pts absolute, OOM/sample > 0.1% during burn-in
00:02:38 Ethan: those numbers sound reasonable as starting defaults, we can tighten them after a couple experiments
00:02:44 Jamie: good, now smoke test plan — Sofia?
00:02:48 Sofia: i'll do the smoke scripts. plan: 3 buckets — short prompts (<60 tokens), mid-range (60-300), long (>300). for each bucket run 3 runs cold cache, 3 runs warm cache. capture token counts, latency histograms, kv-hit ratio and model logits snapshot for top-k checks. i'll put the runner in staging with a post-run artifact that uploads to the spreadsheet.
00:03:12 Hannah: please include deterministic seeds and pin model revision ID, otherwise QA can't reproduce.
00:03:18 Sofia: yep will pin to model:4x-rc2 and add seeds
00:03:22 Luis: and capture config: batch size, quantization flag, route ID — we had missing route metadata last time
00:03:28 Sofia: noted
00:03:30 Jamie: how long will the smoke run take?
00:03:33 Sofia: the full matrix maybe 3-4 hours, but i'll run a quick single-pass smoke in 30 mins to catch obvious regressions
00:03:40 Marcus: for canary burn-in we need continuous load for 48 hours, but we should run a preliminary 6-hour soak to validate metrics pipeline first
00:03:49 Priya: provisioning note: there is a spot on our dedicated fleet where kernel fallback telemetry was flaky last quarter; I'll avoid that host class for canary and pin GPU SKU explicitly
00:03:58 Jamie: good catch, let's avoid the flaky hosts
00:04:01 Ethan: question: who owns the regression blocker decision? product or infra? last time we had cross-ownership confusion
00:04:08 Marcus: operationally SRE triggers rollbacks based on SLO alarms, but product signs off on quality signals. so both: SRE executes rollback, product owns signal definitions and whether signal maps to hard block.
00:04:21 Jamie: let's codify that: product owns the signal set and thresholds, SRE owns automation and execution. add to playbook. agreed?
00:04:28 All: agreed
00:04:31 Hannah: testing note — we'll need a small labeled prompt set for hallucination checks, can product supply 50 high-signal prompts?
00:04:38 Ethan: yes PM will create a 50 prompt set with expected answers and fuzzy matching rules, will hand to QA by next Wednesday
00:04:45 Jamie: great. next, fallback behavior — what do we do on partial capacity degradation?
00:04:51 Priya: runtime supports model variant fallback and per-route lower-latency model substitution. playbook should prefer degraded-mode substitution over full rollback when quality stays acceptable and latency is the only issue. but if hallucination rises, we rollback.
00:05:05 Marcus: also we should define graceful degradation thresholds so apps can show "degraded mode" to end users rather than failures. that requires a header in the response or an error code we standardize on.
00:05:15 Luis: add a route-level config: fallback_model and fallback_percentage. default fallback percentage 0, can increase to 20% then 50% during gradual ramp if we need to shed load.
00:05:24 Priya: agreed, we'll implement a rollout policy in the runtime layer: percentage-based rollout with probe windows and automatic fallback to previous model when regressions detected
00:05:33 Sofia: a practical ask — can the runtime expose per-route token billing estimate so product can see cost delta during canary?
00:05:40 Marcus: yes we can emit token-level cost telemetry, but need RBAC to prevent wide access to raw cost data; we'll add a read-only dashboard link for PM and Release leads
00:05:50 Jamie: ok, compliance question — any legal or audit logs we need to consider for this rollout? Luis?
00:05:55 Luis: audit logs for who triggered canary and rollback must be present, and all model revisions used should be recorded in the deployment artifact. we should also snapshot KMS key id if private deployments are involved.
00:06:06 Jamie: good. now handoff and docs — what docs are required to close the loop?
00:06:10 Priya: playbook in confluence, canary checklist (checkboxes for telemetry, config, model pinning), regression signoff doc, and a short runbook for manual rollback
00:06:18 Hannah: also a QA rubric with labeled prompts and pass criteria and a template for the smoke test spreadsheet
00:06:24 Jamie: timeline recap: quick smoke by Sofia in 48 hours, playbook draft from me by next Monday, canary provisioned by Marcus the week after, burn-in to start 2027-06-08, product signoff after HQ regression pass — that meet folks' calendars?
00:06:38 Ethan: yes, we'll try to compress but okay
00:06:41 Marcus: one operational caveat — if the canary shows intermittent kernel fallback above 1% we should not proceed to 50% until we root-cause; that was painful last time
00:06:51 Priya: I'll add sentinel alerts for kernel fallback rate and memory pressure spikes to the canary policy
00:06:58 Sofia: small nit: please include the model-serving config bits in the smoke test artifact: quantization flag and batch-create TTL and kv cache warmup period
00:07:07 Hannah: QA will start running labeled prompts as soon as Sofia's quick smoke has artifacts; we'll aim to finish labeling within 48 hours of smoke completion
00:07:15 Jamie: wrap-up — who owns what (recap): Jamie playbook + Confluence; Sofia smoke + artifacts; Ethan regression metrics + prompt set; Priya runtime config + eviction thresholds; Marcus canary provisioning + telemetry; Hannah QA labeling; Luis release checklist and audit logs. any missing?
00:07:33 All: no
00:07:35 Jamie: cool. any final blockers?
00:07:37 Marcus: only that we should reserve some burst capacity for rollback lanes — I'll talk to capacity planning to carve 2 machines as a runway
00:07:46 Priya: and i'll avoid the flaky host class in the reservation
00:07:50 Jamie: excellent. let's do a quick run of some Q&A and then sign off
00:07:55 Ethan: one question on metrics — how often should we sample p99 during burn-in? every minute or 5 minutes?
00:08:01 Marcus: 1 minute granularity for p95/p99 during canary, aggregated to 5 minute windows for dashboard and alerts
00:08:09 Hannah: and artifact retention? QA needs at least 30 days of smoke artifacts for audit
00:08:14 Luis: we'll keep artifacts for 90 days for now, until release is complete
00:08:20 Jamie: ok last thing — Slack channel for the rollout? create #rollout-4x-onramp and add relevant folks
00:08:27 Luis: i'll create it and invite everyone
00:08:30 Jamie: cool. thanks all, meeting adjourned

--- End transcript ---
